nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of Fe-doped NiMoO4
nodes.procedure: We firstly fabricated the quadrangular Fe-doped NiMoO4·(xH2O) nanopillar arrays on nickel foam (NF) by hydrothermal method using Ni(NO3)2, (NH4)3MoO7 and FeCl2 aqueous solutions as precursors by gradually increasing the amount of FeCl2 (samples 2#–5#) and prepared sample 1# without adding FeCl2 as a control. The preparation details can be seen in ESI.
nodes.source_text: To obtain the hierarchical NiMoFe NPs@MoO2 NPAs, we firstly fabricated the quadrangular Fe-doped NiMoO4·(xH2O) nanopillar arrays on nickel foam (NF) by hydrothermal method using Ni(NO3)2, (NH4)3MoO7 and FeCl2 aqueous solutions as precursors... We obtained samples 2#–5# by gradually increasing the amount of FeCl2 and prepared sample 1# without adding FeCl2 as a control.

nodes.name: Reductive annealing
nodes.procedure: Then the dense nanoparticles were obtained on the nano-pillar surface through 2 hours annealing under argon/hydrogen (v/v, 5/95) atmosphere at 500 °C.

nodes.source_text: Then the dense nanoparticles were obtained on the nano-pillar surface through 2 hours annealing under argon/hydrogen (v/v, 5/95) atmosphere at 500 °C (Fig. 1 a–c, S1c and d†).

nodes.source_text: Sample 2# can deliver current densities of 10, 100, 200, 500 mA cm⁻² at ultra-low overpotentials of 24, 63, 83, 130 mV, respectively... sample 4# needs 24, 79, 116, 190 mV overpotentials... The NiMoFe NPs@MoO₂ NPAs also show small Tafel slopes ranging from 33 to 43 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH (sample 4#||4#)
nodes.source_text: the two-electrode cell delivers the industrially relevant current densities of 100 and 1000 mA cm⁻² at record low cell voltages of 1.52 and 1.66 V while maintaining an almost unchanged potential over 1000 h water splitting.

chronopotentiometry test at five constant current densities of 10, 100, 200, 500 and 10 mA cm⁻² for a total period of 140 hours. We found that the real-time potential presents a negligible increase during continuous long-time operation
sample 4# shows an almost unchanged overpotential during the 120 hours test under constant current densities of 10, 200, 500, 200 and 10 mA cm⁻²
can maintain a good electrocatalytic activity at the current density of 100 mA cm⁻² over 1000 h without obvious degradation (2.4%)

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show dense NiMoFe nanoparticles on MoO2 nano-pillar arrays with average nanoparticle size of 39 nm and number density of 34 billion cm^-2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average size of the nanoparticles of sample 4# is determined to be 39 nm and the number density of nanoparticles is as high as 34 billion cm^-2 by measuring the high-resolution scanning electron microscopy (HRSEM) images

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS mapping shows Ni, Mo, Fe and O uniformly distributed on the surface of nano-pillars with surface compositions of 32-35 at% Mo, 25-29 at% Ni, 38-42 at% O, and 0-18 at% Fe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of sample 4# shows that Ni, Mo, Fe and O are uniformly distributed on the surface of the nano-pillars

properties.description: Green-colored EDX elemental map highlighting Ni distribution
Yellow-colored EDX elemental map highlighting Fe distribution

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanoparticles embedded in substrate with HRTEM interplanar distances of 0.34 nm for MoO2 (111) and 0.202 nm for Ni (111); TEM-EDS shows nanoparticles composition Ni89Mo10Fe1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the high-resolution TEM images show, the 0.34 nm interplanar distance of the nano-pillar sample is close to that of MoO2 (111)... the 0.202 nm interplanar distance of the nanoparticles is close to that of Ni (111)

properties.description: Grayscale transmission electron microscopy image of nanoparticle with 25 nm scale bar

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows three peaks shifted to lower angles from Ni (JCPDS no. 04-0850) indicating Mo and Fe substituted Ni-based solid-solution alloy with larger lattice parameters, plus MoO2 peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a, the XRD patterns present three peaks close to that of typical Ni (JCPDS no. 04-0850). However, all three peaks shift toward lower angles, indicating larger lattice parameters

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows bulk composition of sample 4# as Ni71Mo25Fe4 after dissolving NiMo(Fe) nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ICP-OES results showed that the composition of sample 1-5# was Ni73Mo23, Ni76Mo23.9Fe0.1, Ni71Mo27Fe2, Ni71Mo25Fe4 and Ni54-Mo31Fe15, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS after 30s Ar+ bombardment shows metallic Ni (852.2, 869.3 eV), metallic Mo (229.3, 231.5 eV), metallic Fe (706.6, 719.8 eV) from NiMoFe nanoparticles and MoOx from MoO2 substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The annealed sample and the sample after the HER test were bombarded by argon-ion for 30 seconds to clean the oxide layer naturally formed on the surface before testing... The high-resolution XPS spectra demonstrate the formation of metallic Ni (peaks at 852.2 eV and 869.3 eV), Mo (peaks at 229.3 and 231.5 eV) and Fe (peaks at 706.6 and 719.8 eV) after annealing

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows MoO2 peaks at 205, 228, 347, 362, 459, 497, 566, 742 cm^-1 at OC; metallic state stable under HER; NiOOH and MoO4^2- form under OER conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After annealing, the sample shows a series of strong Raman peaks of MoO2 at 205, 228, 347, 362, 459, 497, 566, 742 cm^-1 at open circuit (OC) potential
